title: The laam in the Name Allah, and the Al-Ghashiyah recitation check: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Ghashiyah, the makharij and the rules of laam
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 18 (Pupil PDF worksheet: The laam in the Name Allah, and the Al-Ghashiyah recitation check rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 18. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

head: Not this
This
rows: Bismillaah with a full, heavy laam
Bismillaah: light laam after the kasrah

questions.a: Heavy: the haa before has a dammah.

questions.q: Al-Ghashiyah recitation check: recite to the teacher one by one against the rubric. While waiting, mark heavy or light for six examples of the Name Allah on the pupil PDF.
questions.a: Teacher records rubric scores and a target. Sheet: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ H, بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ L, فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ H, لِلَّهِ L, رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ H, نَارُ ٱللَّهِ H.

questions.q: Extend: find the Name Allah in Al-Ikhlas and say heavy or light each time.
questions.a: 112:1 هُوَ ٱللَّهُ heavy; 112:2 ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ heavy (starting).

questions.q: Stretch: in «رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ» (91:13) is the laam heavy or light? Why?
questions.a: Heavy: the laam of rasoolu has a dammah.
A) Light, after kasrah. The meem before has a kasrah, so the laam of Allah is light.

questions.q: Think again: We say 'Bismillah' with a light laam but 'Qul huwa Allah' with a full one. What decides it?
questions.a: The vowel before the Name: after kasrah it is light; after fathah or dammah (or starting with it) it is heavy.
